title: Existence of non-$(0,d-1)$-scribable polytopes
statement: A $d$-polytope is a polytope of dimension $d$, and a polytope is **$(0,d-1)$-scribable** if it has a realization whose vertices lie on a sphere and whose facets are tangent to a concentric sphere. **The non-$(0,d-1)$-scribability conjecture.** For $d>3$, there are $d$-polytopes that are not $(0,d-1)$-scribable. The authors believe this is true but do not construct examples; projectively unique polytopes or polytopes with constrained realization spaces may provide a strategy, though the known families are essentially inscribable.
source_name: Hao Chen and Arnau Padrol, “Scribability problems for polytopes”, arXiv:1508.03537 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.03537

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).
